headline.text: In Kainuun hyvinvointialue, crude shares for curative and life-prolonging treatment and recorded multidisciplinary team meetings lag national benchmarks, while crude symptomatic treatment is higher.

details.text: Among new lung cancer patients in 2019–2023, the county's crude curative treatment share is 20.8% (95% CI 16.0–26.6; n=47/226) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 18.6% (95% CI 14.1–24.2; n=42/226) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, with 95% confidence intervals excluding national values.

Conversely, the crude symptomatic treatment share is 48.2% (95% CI 41.8–54.7; n=109/226) compared with 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally, where the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value across these overlapping treatment categories.

A multidisciplinary team meeting is recorded for a crude 0.9% (95% CI 0.2–3.2; n=2/226) of county patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally—an interval excluding the national value that reflects recording practice rather than care—while the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.3% (95% CI 22.9–34.5; n=64/226), whose interval includes 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally.

headline.text: County treatment gaps are statistically distinct in crude registry data, but public data omit key pathway stages and adjustment for age or stage.

details.text: Reading the crude 28.3% (95% CI 22.9–34.5; n=64/226) share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—as a data-quality signal, we infer that because its 95% confidence interval includes the 27.5% (4089/14873) national value, lower crude curative shares are unlikely to be only a recording artefact, though unrecorded treatment may partly contribute.

County shares are crude (unadjusted for age or stage): stage at diagnosis is often missing nationally, a journal article finds about 90% hospital discharge diagnosis concordance with the Cancer Registry, and digitised Kuva 16 age-adjusted curative figures (about ±0.5 percentage points) provide only national reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women.

Public registry data do not capture symptom onset, referral dates, imaging waits, or exact specialist visit and treatment start dates, while outpatient primary care visits are not included in the report's data and occupational health is unmentioned.

Preliminary, unpublished figures from an MOT study indicate that lung cancer care in Finland takes 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment (versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark), including 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: The team recommends tracking access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance, standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination, and auditing stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary meeting recording completeness.

details.text: Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance (for 16 cancers) with handover alerts while the roadmap plans target times in 2026–2028 and the Filha diagnostics guideline is due before the 2030 interim evaluation.

Since mentor insight indicates a weak referral gets a lower specialist urgency rating and the roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and coordinator guidance in 2026–2028, the team recommends a referral template and a persistent-symptoms pulmonologist referral rule after a normal X-ray—modelled on the KYS regional pathway document—plus a diagnostic-phase contact person, which reviewed regional pathway documents lack.

With multidisciplinary team meetings recorded for a crude 0.9% (95% CI 0.2–3.2; n=2/226) of county patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and stage often missing nationally, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary coding while a national quality registry targeting 90% coverage including stage is planned.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
